subtype: Sharing tasks in a student group [Actor]
passage:
Sunaina: ok group, the presentation. honestly it's faster if I just do all the slides
Farida: I can take the survey results section?
Sunaina: it's fine, I'll do it, I know what I want
Farida: ok...
Sunaina: (three days later, 1 am) I have 22 slides done and I'm dying 😩
Farida: you didn't let anyone help!
Sunaina: I know. and nobody knows what's in it
Sunaina: new plan. names next to sections: Farida results, Rohit intro, Meera references, me the rest. check-in Thursday 5 pm, everyone shows what they have
Farida: yes. I'll start tonight
Rohit: on it

qa.q: What time is the check-in on Thursday?
qa.a: The check-in is Thursday at 5 pm.

qa.q: How does Sunaina feel at 1 a.m. with twenty-two slides?
qa.a: Sunaina feels exhausted and regretful, joking about dying, and sees that doing everything alone left nobody knowing what is in the slides.

qa.q: What did Sunaina change in the new plan?
qa.a: Sunaina put a name next to each section and agreed one shared check-in on Thursday, so every member has a clear job and a checkpoint.

qa.q: How might Farida have felt when Sunaina said “it's fine, I'll do it”?
qa.a: Farida probably felt sidelined and a little deflated, even though Farida had offered, which is why the reply was a hesitant “ok...”.

grounding: A group leader takes everything, then splits the work with clear owners and one agreed checkpoint.

subtype: Sharing tasks in a student group [Actor]
passage: At the polytechnic in the small town, Anand gave each group member a piece of the project on a slip of paper and said, “Bring it when it's done.” No date, no check-in. Ojas got the wiring diagram and kept it in a notebook, meaning to start. Three others worked with quiet resentment, since Anand had kept the best part, the model, for himself. A week later Anand asked who had finished. Only two hands went up. Ojas had not started, and now felt embarrassed and stayed away from the lab. Anand stared at the empty slot in the plan, at the model that lacked wires, and understood that he had handed out jobs but no way of knowing how they were going.

qa.q: What did Ojas get from Anand?
Why did Ojas stay away from the lab?
qa.a: Ojas had not started and felt embarrassed, and avoiding the lab was easier than facing the group.

qa.q: What could Anand do now to rescue the project?
qa.a: Sit with Ojas, agree a small first step and one date, and set a shared check-in for the whole group.

qa.q: How might the other three group members feel about how the work was split?
qa.a: They probably feel resentful, since Anand kept the best part, and unsure how their own pieces fit, because there was no check-in.

grounding: A group leader hands out pieces with no check-in, so members resent the load or vanish.
